"Repo: https://github.com/sairam0424/anvilry
Commit: 1beefe1303e9e562e47a33ed654d322f99a99a30 (already checked out in this directory, deps installed, run with `pnpm dev`)

Attached screenshots, all from a 390px-wide phone:
1. 1_about_page_bottom_390px.png - /about scrolled to the bottom
2. 2_menu_open_390px.png - /about with the hamburger menu open
3. 3_chat_view_390px.png - the chat view (/?view=chat)

I tested the site on my phone and found these problems:

1. The floating \"Ask my portfolio\" and ⌘K buttons cover real content. At the bottom of /about they sit on top of the footer links (you can't read or tap \"Subscribe\"), and in the chat view the ⌘K button covers the small print under the message box. Content should never end up hidden behind these buttons on phones, on any page or view.
2. When the mobile menu is open, the rest of the page isn't dimmed and tapping outside the menu doesn't close it. It should behave like a normal mobile menu: dim the page behind it and close when you tap outside.
3. In the chat view, the row with \"Back to Classic / Résumé / Talk / AI Concierge\" doesn't fit: \"AI Concierge\" is cut off at the right edge.

Please find the root cause of each and fix them properly, without changing how things look on desktop. Then check the result in a browser at 390px and 320px (and at desktop width) and show me what you verified."

**Analyzing the User Prompt**

I'm carefully dissecting the user's prompt. I've noted the specified repository, commit hash, and the instruction to run the project. I'm also paying close attention to the attached screenshots, which I understand are relevant to the user's issue. The screenshots will need further scrutiny.


**Identifying Mobile Issues**

I've pinpointed several mobile-specific layout problems. The "Ask my portfolio" and ⌘K buttons are obscuring content on both the /about page and chat view, which is undesirable. The mobile menu doesn't dim the background or close on outside taps, and the "AI Concierge" text is cut off in the chat view. I need to make these mobile-responsive changes while preserving the desktop display.

todos.content: Inspect git status, workspace files, and find relevant components
Investigate Issue 1: Floating buttons covering content at bottom of pages/views
Investigate Issue 2: Mobile menu backdrop dimming and tap outside to close
Investigate Issue 3: Chat view top bar overflowing/cut off on mobile
Implement fixes for all 3 issues ensuring no regressions on desktop
Verify in browser at 390px, 320px, and desktop width

6:

8: 
9: ## Commands
10: 
11: ```bash
12: # Development
13: pnpm install
14: pnpm dev                   # starts Velite watch + Next.js dev @ localhost:3000
15: 
16: # Build (Velite + tests + Next.js, in that order)
17: pnpm build
18:

20: # is Turbopack, which @next/bundle-analyzer cannot hook. Writes .next/analyze/{client,edge,nodejs}.html.
21: # NOTE: a --webpack build does NOT emit .next/diagnostics/route-bundle-stats.json, so
22: # `node scripts/bundle-budget.mjs` correctly fails after this — re-run `pnpm build` before the gate.
23: pnpm analyze               # velite --clean && ANALYZE=true next build --webpack
24: 
25: # Testing
26: pnpm test                  # vitest run once
27: pnpm test:watch            # vitest interactive watch mode
28: npx vitest run src/lib/llm.test.ts          # single file
29: npx vitest run -t "corpus"                  # single test by name

31: # Lint
32: pnpm lint                  # eslint (flat config, no --fix by default)
33: 
34: # Content regeneration (when MDX changes aren't picked up by watch)
35: pnpm content               # velite --clean
36: 
37: # After build: generate Pagefind search index
38: # NOTE: this is a Makefile target only — there is NO `pnpm search-index` script.
39: make search-index          # == pnpm pagefind --site .next/server/app --output-path public/pagefind
40: 
41: # Cache wipe (all build artifacts)
42: pnpm clean
43: 
44: # Makefile convenience wrappers
45: make dev / make build / make test / make lint
46: make new-work SLUG=my-case-study     # scaffold work MDX
47: make new-project SLUG=my-oss-repo    # scaffold project MDX
48: make new-note SLUG=my-note           # scaffold note MDX
49: make new-article SLUG=my-post        # scaffold article MDX
50: make health                          # smoke-test /api/chat locally
51: make trace TRACE_ID=abc123           # replay a request from Redis telemetry
52: make deploy-prod                     # vercel deploy --prod
53: ```
54: 
55: ### Extended Makefile Targets
56: 
57: ```bash
58: # Environment
59: make env-check             # audit which env vars are set (Bedrock, Redis, GCP TTS, admin, flags)
60: make env-setup             # step-by-step guide to bootstrap .env.local
61: make env-vercel            # pull Vercel production vars into local .env.local
62: 
63: # Feature flags
64: make flags-show            # print all NEXT_PUBLIC_* flags + current values
65: make flags-beast           # print unlock commands for all visual effects (orb bloom, ink, skill tree)
66: make flags-notes-on / flags-notes-off  # toggle /notes section on Vercel
67: 
68: # Observability
69: make logs                  # stream Vercel runtime logs
70: make logs-llm              # stream logs, grep LLM lines
71: make admin                 # open /admin/telemetry in browser
72: 
73: # Deployment / git
74: make deploy-preview        # trigger manual Vercel preview
75: make rollback              # rollback to previous Vercel deployment
76: make pr                    # open PR: current branch → develop
77: make pr-prod               # open PR: develop → main
78: make push                  # push current branch
79: 
80: # Content management
81: make resume-list / resume-open   # manage PDFs in public/resume/
82: ```
83: 
84: ---
85: 
86: ## Branch Model & CI
87: 
88: **Branch topology:**
89: - `develop` — integration branch; all feature work targets this; Vercel Preview deploys
90: - `main` — production release branch; merged from `develop` only; Vercel Production deploys
91: 
92: **CI pipeline (`.github/workflows/`) — three workflows:**
93: - `ci.yml` — runs on every push + PRs to `develop`/`main`: lint → typecheck (`tsc --noEmit`) → `pnpm test`. Generates `.velite/` before typecheck and vitest — this mirrors the production build order and is required because `.velite/` is gitignored. Its `e2e` job also runs the **bundle budget** gate (`.github/workflows/ci.yml:110-111` → `scripts/bundle-budget.mjs`) immediately after its existing Build step, so it rides on that build rather than adding a second one.
94: - `codeql.yml` — static JavaScript/TypeScript analysis on `develop` **and `main`** pushes/PRs + weekly.
95:   `main` is listed on purpose: a hotfix pushed straight to it used to deploy with no analysis.
96: - `dependency-review.yml` — dependency security check on PRs.
97: 
98: **Bundle budget gate.** `scripts/bundle-budget.mjs` reads `.next/diagnostics/route-bundle-stats.json` — written by `next build` with no flag, but **only under Turbopack** — and asserts two things: every route's first-load JS stays under `MAX_FIRST_LOAD_BYTES` (`scripts/bundle-budget.mjs:45`; largest today is `/` at 1,220,794 B, so ~5% headroom), and three.js stays **off** the first-load critical path (marker-based on `WebGLRenderer`, `scripts/bundle-budget.mjs:57`). A missing or malformed artifact exits 1 by design. The CI step deliberately carries **no** `continue-on-error` and **no** `if-no-files-found` — unmeasurable must mean red.
99: 
100: **`bundle-analysis.yml` is DELETED — do not re-add it.** It was green and empty for its entire life: 222 runs, 211 green, zero artifacts across the 25 most recent. Three independent causes, each sufficient. (1) `next build` in Next 16 is **Turbopack**, not webpack (`node_modules/next/dist/lib/bundler.js:142-144` — "The default is turbopack when nothing is configured" — sets `TURBOPACK='auto'`), and `@next/bundle-analyzer` is webpack-only: it prints "not compatible with Turbopack builds, no report will be generated" and returns a config whose `.webpack` is undefined, so the `ANALYZE=true` build produced nothing. The workflow's own comment asserted the opposite; that assertion was **false**. (2) The `nextjs-bundle-analysis` compare step (last published 2023) reads the Pages-Router `build-manifest.json.pages`, which is `{"/_app": []}` in this App Router app — even fully wired it emits `{"raw":0,"gzip":0}`, i.e. "this PR introduced no changes to the JavaScript bundle" on every PR forever. (3) `if-no-files-found: warn` plus `continue-on-error: true` made both failures invisible. `develop` is not branch-protected, so nothing required it.

make env-vercel            # pull Vercel production vars into local .env.local

# Feature flags
make flags-show            # print all NEXT_PUBLIC_* flags + current values
make flags-beast           # print unlock commands for all visual effects (orb bloom, ink, skill tree)
make flags-notes-on / flags-notes-off  # toggle /notes section on Vercel

# Observability
make logs                  # stream Vercel runtime logs
make logs-llm              # stream logs, grep LLM lines
make admin                 # open /admin/telemetry in browser

# Deployment / git
make deploy-preview        # trigger manual Vercel preview
make rollback              # rollback to previous Vercel deployment
make pr                    # open PR: current branch → develop
make pr-prod               # open PR: develop → main
make push                  # push current branch

# Content management
make resume-list / resume-open   # manage PDFs in public/resume/
```

---

## Branch Model & CI

**Branch topology:**
- `develop` — integration branch; all feature work targets this; Vercel Preview deploys
- `main` — production release branch; merged from `develop` only; Vercel Production deploys

**CI pipeline (`.github/workflows/`) — three workflows:**
- `ci.yml` — runs on every push + PRs to `develop`/`main`: lint → typecheck (`tsc --noEmit`) → `pnpm test`. Generates `.velite/` before typecheck and vitest — this mirrors the production build order and is required because `.velite/` is gitignored. Its `e2e` job also runs the **bundle budget** gate (`.github/workflows/ci.yml:110-111` → `scripts/bundle-budget.mjs`) immediately after its existing Build step, so it rides on that build rather than adding a second one.
- `codeql.yml` — static JavaScript/TypeScript analysis on `develop` **and `main`** pushes/PRs + weekly.
  `main` is listed on purpose: a hotfix pushed straight to it used to deploy with no analysis.
- `dependency-review.yml` — dependency security check on PRs.

**Bundle budget gate.** `scripts/bundle-budget.mjs` reads `.next/diagnostics/route-bundle-stats.json` — written by `next build` with no flag, but **only under Turbopack** — and asserts two things: every route's first-load JS stays under `MAX_FIRST_LOAD_BYTES` (`scripts/bundle-budget.mjs:45`; largest today is `/` at 1,220,794 B, so ~5% headroom), and three.js stays **off** the first-load critical path (marker-based on `WebGLRenderer`, `scripts/bundle-budget.mjs:57`). A missing or malformed artifact exits 1 by design. The CI step deliberately carries **no** `continue-on-error` and **no** `if-no-files-found` — unmeasurable must mean red.

**`bundle-analysis.yml` is DELETED — do not re-add it.** It was green and empty for its entire life: 222 runs, 211 green, zero artifacts across the 25 most recent. Three independent causes, each sufficient. (1) `next build` in Next 16 is **Turbopack**, not webpack (`node_modules/next/dist/lib/bundler.js:142-144` — "The default is turbopack when nothing is configured" — sets `TURBOPACK='auto'`), and `@next/bundle-analyzer` is webpack-only: it prints "not compatible with Turbopack builds, no report will be generated" and returns a config whose `.webpack` is undefined, so the `ANALYZE=true` build produced nothing. The workflow's own comment asserted the opposite; that assertion was **false**. (2) The `nextjs-bundle-analysis` compare step (last published 2023) reads the Pages-Router `build-manifest.json.pages`, which is `{"/_app": []}` in this App Router app — even fully wired it emits `{"raw":0,"gzip":0}`, i.e. "this PR introduced no changes to the JavaScript bundle" on every PR forever. (3) `if-no-files-found: warn` plus `continue-on-error: true` made both failures invisible. `develop` is not branch-protected, so nothing required it.

# Skill: dev-local

# Anvilry dev-local launcher

One-command local dev stack for Anvilry. Single Next.js app with Velite content processing.

## Service / Port Map

| Service | Port | Notes |
|---------|------|-------|
| Next.js dev server | 3000 | All four views: classic / chat / game / terminal |

## Prerequisites
- Node 22+ and pnpm installed
- `.env.local` exists (run `vercel env pull .env.local` to pull from Vercel)
- `pnpm install` has been run

## Commands

### up — start the dev stack
```bash
cd /Users/sairamugge/Desktop/Not-Humans-World/Anvilry/sairam-dev
pnpm dev
```
This runs `velite --watch & next dev` — Velite watches MDX content in `content/` and Next.js
serves at `localhost:3000`. The `predev` script runs Velite once synchronously before Next.js
starts so types are ready.

### verify — smoke-test the running stack
```bash
curl -s http://localhost:3000 | grep -q "Sairam" && echo "OK" || echo "FAIL"
curl -s http://localhost:3000/api/chat -X POST \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}]}' \

### content — regenerate Velite output (when MDX changes not picked up)

cd /Users/sairamugge/Desktop/Not-Humans-World/Anvilry/sairam-dev
pnpm content
```

### test — run the test suite
```bash
cd /Users/sairamugge/Desktop/Not-Humans-World/Anvilry/sairam-dev
pnpm test
```

### build — full production build (Velite + tests + Next.js)
```bash
cd /Users/sairamugge/Desktop/Not-Humans-World/Anvilry/sairam-dev
pnpm build
```

parts.text:
### Root Causes

1. **Floating buttons covering bottom content:**
   - **Root Cause:** `AskPortfolio` (`bottom-5 left-5`) and `CommandPalette` (`bottom-5 right-5`) are `fixed` floating action buttons ~35–42px tall, sitting 20px off the viewport bottom. In `SiteFooter`, the bottom strip had only `pb-6` (24px) padding, so at the scroll end, copyright and "Subscribe" / "RSS" links sat directly behind the buttons. In `ChatView`, `<main>` is viewport-height constrained (`h-[calc(100dvh-3.5rem)]`) with `py-6` (24px padding), placing the composer and its bottom caption (`Grounded in real work · may simplify details`) right across the bottom margin where the ⌘K button overlaps it. In addition, when 8 chips wrapped vertically on very short viewports like 320×568, they expanded downward and pushed the composer into the bottom margin.

2. **Mobile menu undimmed & tap-outside not working:**
   - **Root Cause:** In `SiteNav`, `<header>` has `backdrop-blur-md` and `style={{ viewTransitionName: "site-header" }}`. Under CSS specs, both `backdrop-filter` and `view-transition-name` establish a containing block for `fixed` descendants. Because `MobileNav` rendered its backdrop `div` (`fixed inset-0 top-14`) inside `<header>` (which is only 56px tall), the backdrop was constrained to `<header>`'s 56px height, collapsing to 0px height (`top: 56px; bottom: 0;`). The dimming overlay never covered the document, and clicks outside the menu panel could never reach the backdrop.

3. **Chat view top bar cut off:**
   - **Root Cause:** In `ChatView`, the top bar is a non-wrapping flex container (`flex items-center justify-between gap-3`). Its children—`ViewEscapeHatch` ("Back to Classic" + "Résumé", intrinsic width ~218px) and the right group ("Talk" + "AI Concierge", intrinsic width ~187px)—total ~417px with gaps. On mobile screens (390px width has 342px content space; 320px width has 272px), 417px exceeds available width. Without `flex-wrap`, the right side was pushed past the screen edge, clipping "AI Concierge".

---

### Fixes Applied

- **`src/components/site-footer.tsx`:** Updated the bottom strip's padding to `pb-24 sm:pb-6`. On mobile viewports (< 640px), 96px of bottom padding lifts the copyright, "Subscribe", and "RSS" links well above the floating action buttons. On desktop (`sm:`), the original `pb-6` (24px) is preserved.
- **`src/components/chat/chat-view.tsx`:**
  - Updated `<main>` padding to `px-6 pt-6 pb-20 sm:pb-6`, lifting the console box and caption text safely above the ⌘K button on mobile while leaving desktop unchanged.
  - Added `flex-wrap`, `gap-y-2 gap-x-3`, `ml-auto sm:ml-0`, and `shrink-0` on "AI Concierge" to the top escape-hatch/status row so it wraps cleanly onto two lines on mobile without clipping, while remaining on a single row on desktop.
  - Added `max-h-28 sm:max-h-none overflow-y-auto` to the chip container to prevent chips from pushing controls on compact viewports.
- **`src/components/game/developer-view.tsx` & `game-view.tsx`:** Added `pb-24 sm:pb-6` on `developer-view` and `flex-wrap gap-y-2 gap-x-3` to top rows to protect terminal clearance and prevent truncation on narrow screens.
- **`src/components/view-escape-hatch.tsx`:** Added `flex-wrap` to allow the button pair to wrap gracefully on ultra-compact screens.
- **`src/components/mobile-nav.tsx`:**
  - Portalled the backdrop and drawer panel to `document.body` via `createPortal`, freeing the backdrop from `<header>`'s containing block so it covers the full viewport (`top-14` to bottom) with `bg-bg-base/80 backdrop-blur-sm`.
  - Added `onClick` dismissal on backdrop tap, background scroll lock (`document.body.style.overflow = "hidden"`), view-switch dismissal via `useView`, and responsive cleanup on desktop resize (`lg:hidden`).
- **`src/components/mobile-nav.dom.test.tsx`:** Added unit tests verifying portal rendering, dimming backdrop presence, tap-outside closing, Escape closing, and link navigation closing.

---

### Verification Results

Ran automated headless browser tests with Playwright across 390px, 320px, and desktop (1280px):

| Check | 390px (iPhone 13/14) | 320px (iPhone SE) | Desktop (1280px) |
|---|---|---|---|
| **/about footer vs floating buttons** | Clear: Subscribe link is 41.2px above ⌘K button; copyright is fully above Ask button | Clear: Subscribe link is 41.2px above ⌘K button; copyright is fully above Ask button | Desktop layout intact, no overlap |
| **Mobile menu backdrop dimming** | Backdrop covers full viewport below header (788px height), dims page with `bg-bg-base/80 backdrop-blur-sm` | Backdrop covers full viewport below header (512px height), dims page with `bg-bg-base/80 backdrop-blur-sm` | Drawer and backdrop hidden on desktop (`lg:hidden`) |
| **Mobile menu tap-outside** | Tap on backdrop at `(195, 487)` closes menu | Tap on backdrop at `(160, 487)` closes menu | N/A (desktop nav used) |
| **Chat top bar ("AI Concierge")** | Right edge at 366px ≤ 390px (0px overflow, fits cleanly on wrapped line 2) | Right edge at 296px ≤ 320px (0px overflow, fits cleanly on wrapped line 2) | Single row: "Back to Classic" / "Résumé" left, "Talk" / "AI Concierge" right |
| **Chat small print vs ⌘K button** | Caption bottom: 743px, ⌘K top: 788.7px (+45.7px clearance) | Caption bottom: 467px, ⌘K top: 512.7px (+45.7px clearance) | ⌘K button sits in desktop gutter, 0 overlap |

All unit tests pass (72/72 files, 597/597 tests), ESLint is clean, bundle budget checks pass, and the production build completes successfully.
